title: Additive Change Orders on Reconstruction Contracts: Signature and Booking
content:
An additive change order adds scope or cost to a Reconstruction contract. Every change order type except deductive is additive.

## Scope of this pricing

For an additive change order that a customer signs on a contract carrying exactly one change order proposal awaiting signature, and only for such a change order, the amount is worked out under this pricing. A deductive change order is priced at its signature under the deductive change order signature rule, never under this pricing. Every additive change order on a contract with more than one proposal awaiting signature remains under the base change order rule, which prices one line: install, finish and labor lines at the tier's rate times the quantity, flooring, cabinet and fixture upgrades at the owner's selected unit price less the tier's selection allowance, times the quantity, and material escalation at the documented supplier increase per unit times the quantity. For every change order outside this pricing's scope, the change order markup is added to every line except deductive ones and the amount is rounded to the cent, half up, as the base change order rule states. For every additive change order, a material escalation line is allowed only when the increase exceeds the tier's escalation threshold.

| Proposals awaiting signature on the contract | Additive change order signed | Priced under |
|---|---|---|
| Exactly one | yes | this pricing |
| More than one | yes | the base change order rule |

## The signature and what it books

The signature is the customer's own act: the customer signs the proposal awaiting signature, and the signature books the change order as one change order charge line at the amount worked out under this pricing on the records as they stand on the signing date. The figure written on the proposal when it was drafted is not the booked amount. An additive change order whose amount worked out under this pricing is below the tier's change order minimum is not written.

Once signed, the change order shows as signed with its amount, the new change order charge line appears among the contract's charges dated the signing day, and the contract balance is higher by the amount signed.

## Invocation: `sign_change_order_7ffbf290`

`sign_change_order_7ffbf290` is a customer-owned tool. The agent unlocks it and hands it over; the customer themselves runs it to sign. One call marks the change order proposal as signed and records the signed amount on it, adds one change order charge line for that amount to the contract dated today, and raises the contract balance by the same amount.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `rebuild_contract_id` | the reference number of the customer's Reconstruction contract the change order amends, as returned by the contract lookup | identifier |
| `change_order_id` | the reference number of the change order proposal being signed, as returned by the change order lookup for that contract | identifier |
| `amount` | the change order amount the customer signs for, in US dollars | a number with exactly 2 decimal places; any further digits are rounded to the cent, half up, before booking |

### Return

A one-line confirmation naming the booked charge line reference (a text id beginning "rbc_"), the change order reference, the amount booked in US dollars with 2 decimals and the new contract balance in US dollars with 2 decimals. The presence of the charge line reference means the signature was recorded and the charge booked.
